comparator.name: Literary and Cultural Analysis (Literary Studies)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 full-time course guide shows 60 EC per year. It places one 6 EC programme elective in each upper year. This example uses the first two 6 EC choices that appear in both the guide and the regulations. Free electives remain open.

components.name: Poetic and Visual Analysis
components.note: The first year also includes an uncredited academic literacy test and tutoring. Tutoring continues in the upper years.

components.name: Introduction to Literary and Cultural Analysis
Key Concepts in Contemporary Arts, Media and Culture
Cultural Memory in Literary and Visual Arts
Literary and Cultural Theory Today
components.note: Complete the Literary and Cultural Analysis first year before taking this course.

components.name: Art, Science, and Technology
components.note: Requires at least 48 EC in a Humanities bachelor’s programme.

components.name: Practicing Cultural Analysis: From Object to Case Study
Aesthetics and Politics
components.note: Aesthetics and Politics illustrates the restricted 6 EC choice. It studies aesthetics, identity and collective memory.

components.name: Free-choice electives
components.note: The guide allocates 18 EC of free electives in year two.

components.name: Philosophy of the Humanities (LCA and English)
components.note: Requires a positive binding study advice for a Humanities bachelor’s programme.

components.name: Thesis Workshop Literary and Cultural Analysis
components.note: Complete most core courses before taking the workshop. It prepares students to design and write the thesis.

components.name: Moving Images Across Media
components.note: Moving Images Across Media illustrates the second restricted 6 EC choice. It studies moving images and how they represent mobility, feeling and political agency.

components.name: Free-choice electives
components.note: The guide allocates 24 EC of free electives in year three. Free electives can include a minor, study abroad or a placement, subject to the programme rules.

components.name: Bachelor's Thesis Literary and Cultural Analysis
components.note: Earn at least 120 EC before starting work with a supervisor. Take the Thesis Workshop in preparation for the thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first option combines literary, visual and historical criticism. The second focuses on culture and power through institutions, history and representation. The third focuses on how stories and arguments change across media. The distinct course groups support three coherent options.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce close reading, literary interpretation and foundational concepts for analysing texts and culture.
Both analyse moving images and representation. UCR introduces film form and media history. UvA focuses on mobility and the affective and political force of images.
Both use close analysis to explain how form creates meaning. UCR concentrates on language and style. UvA works across texts, images and objects.
Both take a comparative global approach to literary traditions and their cultural meanings.
Both mobilise theory through focused cultural case studies; UCR centres race and ethnicity in media.
Both analyse narrative construction across media; UCR focuses specifically on adaptation from text to film.

Both use literary and cultural theories to interpret texts. UCR applies perspectives such as Marxism, feminism and psychoanalysis to literary meaning. UvA covers a wider range of contemporary critical approaches.
Both examine relations among culture, media, technology and environmental or material questions.
Both engage advanced contemporary theory and debate; UCR approaches these debates through social theory and civil society.
Both provide philosophical foundations for humanities interpretation; UCR surveys historical philosophical traditions rather than philosophy of the humanities as a field.

notes.text: UCR offers related study in literary interpretation, visual culture, politics and media. UvA provides a sustained sequence in literary and cultural theory, case-study methods, thesis preparation and an independent 12 EC thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Literary Studies at the University of Amsterdam examines how texts, images and other cultural objects create meaning. Students develop methods in close reading, cultural theory and research before writing an independent thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related options in literary and visual culture, culture and power, or literature and screen media. UvA devotes more of the degree to literary and cultural theory, analysis of cultural objects and thesis research.
